shared_elements: pale weathered limestone as the medium
quadruped animal with elongated snout / bared teeth shown in profile
emphasis on animal subject matter rather than ornament
justification: The clearest correspondence is that both are pale limestone works whose principal motif is a heavy-bodied quadruped with an elongated muzzle and exposed teeth, seen essentially in profile. Everything else diverges: A is a single free-standing figure carved fully in the round with no field or framing, while B is a flat pillar face covered with several stacked registers of low-relief motifs (birds, disc, snake-like line, banded border), so there is no shared compositional scheme or comparable carving technique.
